split_policy.primary_axis: bootstrap-readiness runner behavior before fixture directory label, JSON snapshot, generated timestamp, source label, issue title text, empty blocker report, old-mode label, shim label, fallback label, compatibility label, migration label, or report label
split_policy.positive_rule: bootstrap-readiness-runner positives are limited to hand-authored runner scenarios in this family: zero_open owns accepted zero-input readiness, and blocked_issues owns blocked-input runner handling for issue 1149 without treating the empty open_blockers report as zero-readiness truth
split_policy.canonical_rejection_rule: open issue snapshots promoted to positive zero-readiness, empty open_blockers reports used to erase issue evidence, directory-label-only readiness, runner-only success, workflow-label-only success, generated-only rows, report-only rows, migration-only rows, old-mode rows, shim rows, fallback rows, and compatibility rows are non-positive rejection or provenance evidence
split_policy.strict_error_rule: missing required scenario JSON, blocked_issues ignored by the runner, issue 1149 treated as release-ready, open_blocker_count used as the only readiness dimension, generated/report rows promoted as support, and old-mode/shim/fallback/compat rows promoted as support own fail-closed strict-error evidence
split_policy.provenance_rule: catalog snapshots, issues snapshots, milestones snapshots, open_blockers snapshots, generated_at_utc values, source labels, issue numbers, issue titles, open_blocker_count values, fixture directory names, empty array markers, and owner-split routing rows remain provenance unless an owner split claims the runner behavior boundary
split_policy.retired_surface_rule: old-mode runner rows, shim runner rows, fallback runner rows, compatibility runner rows, migration-only rows, generated-only rows, report-only rows, wrapper-only rows, runner-label-only rows, workflow-label-only rows, empty-report-only rows, and generated/report rows promoted as support are canonical rejection, strict-error, absent-support, or provenance-only evidence
